rationale: NPB IS is a tiny (779 lines, 7 functions, ~3.3KB text) compute-kernel whose runtime is dominated by tight integer loops in rank, create_seq, and full_verify, so the weight table front-loads cheap, layout/data-oriented transforms and throttles control-flow-expansion passes: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain with negligible runtime/size cost since arithmetic substitution is ideal for small hot integer kernels; SPLIT and IBR diversify basic-block structure at low cost and aid SUB/FLA by enlarging blocks; ICALL and IGV add strong static-analysis resistance (indirect call targets and collapsed control-flow graph) at modest overhead; BCF and especially FLA carry high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (FLA also nontrivial CorrectnessRisk on loop-heavy code) so the selector applies them sparingly — only to cold functions like c_print_results — keeping total overhead acceptable while the cheap passes provide broad, diverse obfuscation coverage with near-zero correctness exposure.
